mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during GDP growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 6% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when unemployment is below 6%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and housing starts indicate economic expansion, positively affecting S&P 500.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between industrial production, housing starts, and S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate during tightening may slow economic growth, negatively impacting S&P 500.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns remain positive despite high FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Stable CPI suggests controlled inflation, maintaining consumer and investor confidence.
failure_condition: No positive S&P 500 returns with stable CPI.

mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rate stimulates borrowing and investment, boosting S&P 500.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns do not increase with lower FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in employment and retail sales indicates strong economic activity, positively impacting S&P 500.
failure_condition: No correlation between employment, retail sales, and S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth during late-cycle expansion supports continued economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDP growth does not lead to positive S&P 500 returns.
